anchor_definition: The anchor is the encode-pipeline ENTRY l = function(t){return a(c(o(t)))}: the shallowest function that represents 'the encoding' as a whole, composing the inner stages o (string->bytes), c (transform), a (map to the socialist-values alphabet). PLAN §5.1: the entry is the target-specific value constructor the task asks for; an individual inner stage is only a path step, and the decode entry is off-chain.

anchor.why: The encode entry: composes o, c and a to turn the raw input string into the final encoded output string assigned to the output textarea (p.value = l(v.value)).

roles.why: The final pipeline stage: maps index pairs onto the 24-char alphabet h (富强民主...) producing the visible characters. On the encode path but only one stage, not the entry.
The inverse DECODE entry (reads the alphabet back to bytes). Opposite direction; not on the encode path.
